territorial_scope.description: Applies under the New York State Tax Law to qualified films for the Empire State film production credit.

evidence.quote: The People of the State of New York, represented in Senate and Assembly, do enact as follows:

summary.short: Amends New York Tax Law § 24 to exclude from the qualified-film definition, and so from the Empire State film production credit, any production using AI in a manner that displaces employees whose salaries are qualified expenses, unless a current collective bargaining agreement permits the replacement. Effective immediately.
summary.long: Bill S7422-A (2023-2024 session) amends paragraph 3 of subdivision (b) of section 24 of the New York Tax Law, which defines 'qualified film' for the Empire State film production credit. The amendment adds a new clause (iii) to the list of exclusions from that definition: a production that uses artificial intelligence in a manner resulting in the displacement of employees whose salaries are qualified expenses, unless the replacement is permitted by a current collective bargaining agreement covering those employees. The other exclusions (documentaries, productions requiring 18 U.S.C. § 2257 records, and certain variety series) and the minimum-budget rule are restated unchanged. Section 2 provides that the act takes effect immediately. The bill was introduced in May 2023 and committed to the Senate Committee on Investigations and Government Operations. The text states no penalty, enforcement authority or definition of artificial intelligence; its only operative provision concerns eligibility for the tax credit.
